one_liner: Rust port of C++ P2300 senders/receivers with a mio event loop; its single-threaded echo server beats Tokio 10-26% (self-reported).
what_it_does: exec-rs reimplements the P2300 std::execution model from NVIDIA stdexec in Rust. You describe work as lazy senders (just, then, let_value, when_all, when_any, bulk, repeat_effect_until, and so on), connect them to receivers and start them on schedulers (RunLoop, StaticThreadPool, TrampolineScheduler, timed schedulers). AsyncScope and CountingScope provide structured concurrency. A net module modelled on P2762 adds an IoContext event loop over mio, plus async_accept, async_receive and async_send senders for TCP. It does not replace Tokio: there is no async/await runtime API, though a future bridge (into_future / from_future) converts between senders and Futures.
how_it_is_fast: The echo result comes from a small single-threaded reactor. IoContext::run_one polls mio (epoll/kqueue) and runs readiness callbacks inline on the same thread, so the hot path has no work-stealing scheduler, task wakers or cross-thread handoff. Each read or write is tried directly on the non-blocking socket first. Only on WouldBlock does it store a boxed completion in a per-token HashMap. repeat_effect_until keeps each iteration's operation state inline and uses a thread-local trampoline to bound recursion. The Tokio baseline is not a current_thread runtime: it is Tokio's multi-thread scheduler with worker_threads(1), with the accept loop running inside block_on.
when_to_use: Studying or prototyping P2300/stdexec-style sender pipelines in Rust: then/let_value/when_all/bulk, stop tokens, and async scopes.
Research on how the sender/receiver design compares with Future-based runtimes on allocations and scheduling overhead, since operation states are exposed and kept inline.
A single-threaded, Unix-only TCP request/response loop with trivial per-connection work, where you will re-run the echo benchmark on your own hardware before trusting the gap.
Reading material for porting C++ std::execution code (stdexec, uring_exec) to Rust or comparing the two.
when_not_to_use: Production services. There is no LICENSE file, CI or issue history, the repo has 30 commits and 0 forks, and the author's commit messages describe the January 2026 rewrite as 'Brand new version with vibe coding'.
Multi-core servers. IoContext is single-threaded, and the repo's own examples/echo_server/README.md reports Tokio and exec-rs as 'nearly identical' at 4 threads (3,714k vs 3,703k at 500 connections).

Anything beyond plain TCP: there is no TLS, UDP, DNS, file I/O or I/O-integrated timers, and no ecosystem (hyper, tonic, reqwest). Nested when_all and the merge/transform_each sequence senders are listed as incomplete.
Windows. Sockets are registered with the poller only under cfg(unix).
async/await codebases. Handlers become nested closures that clone Arcs: the exec echo example is 105 lines against 51 for the Tokio one.

integration.form: crate (git dependency only; not published on crates.io under this name)
integration.dependencies: pin-project-lite 0.2, parking_lot 0.12, crossbeam-channel 0.5, wait_on_address 0.1, mio 1 (os-poll, os-ext, net); tokio is a dev-dependency only
integration.min_toolchain: Rust 2021 edition; no rust-version declared. IoContext::spawn uses associated-type-bound syntax (Sender<Completions: ...>), which implies Rust 1.79+ (inferred).
integration.platforms: The core sender/scheduler code is plain Rust. Networking is Unix-only: Linux (epoll) and macOS/BSD (kqueue) through mio, because socket registration is behind cfg(unix). There is no CI, so no platform has been tested.
integration.thread_safety: IoContext is single-threaded. Its poll handle, socket map and pending-op map are RefCells behind `unsafe impl Send + Sync`. Only the atomic intrusive task queue and the mio Waker are safe to use from other threads (through IoContextScheduler). StaticThreadPool and SingleThreadContext are for cross-thread compute.

gotchas: The README's `exec-rs = "0.1"` resolves on crates.io to an unrelated crate (robinfriedli/exec-rs, task-execution utilities, versions 0.1.0-0.2.0). Use a git dependency instead. Cargo.toml's repository field also points to the wrong place (github.com/yuchao/exec-rs).

I/O senders make one non-blocking syscall per readiness event. A spurious wakeup completes with a WouldBlock error instead of retrying, and repeat_effect/repeat_effect_until stop on error, so one spurious wakeup can end the accept loop or a connection.

async_send_from does a single write and the echo example ignores the byte count, so partial writes are silently dropped (Tokio's echo uses write_all). IoContext keeps one pending op per socket token, so a concurrent read and write on one socket overwrite each other.

Resource handling is loose. TcpStream has no Drop impl and deregister_socket is never called in the net module, so socket-map entries build up per connection. IoContext::spawn deliberately leaks the operation ('For now, we leak it'). The README calls StaticThreadPool work-stealing, but it is one shared crossbeam bounded channel.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick exec-rs only if you want P2300 sender/receiver semantics in Rust specifically; uring_exec is the more serious C++ equivalent (P2300-style over io_uring). If you just need to beat Tokio, monoio (thread-per-core io_uring, about 1.86x Tokio at 4 cores in its own benchmark) and ringline are far more complete.
verified_claims_summary: The top-level README table compares a single-threaded exec_echo (mio loop) with Tokio's multi-thread runtime at worker_threads(1). Results were 114,723 vs 104,601 req/s (50 connections), 130,694 vs 114,478 (200), 135,157 vs 107,333 (500) and 100,321 vs 85,745 (4 KB), which is +10% to +26%. benchmark.sh shows the load came from haraldh/rust_echo_bench on 127.0.0.1: one blocking client thread per connection, 128 B messages, 10 s, with 'Large' being 100 connections of 4096 B. No CPU, OS, rustc version or run count is given. The script launches a nonexistent 'exec_echo_async' example, and the example directory's own README (Linux 5.15) reports only +4-7% single-threaded and parity at 4 threads.
status_note: The last commit was 2026-01-31, about 8 months ago, so 'active' is generous. The current code is a January 2026 rewrite. README and Cargo.toml say Apache-2.0 but the repo has no LICENSE file, so read it for reference and do not take it as a dependency.
